task_objective: Make Trivy scan exact-tag source dependencies as well as release artifacts, and enable Semgrep with a vendored advisory ruleset.
design_decisions: Trivy scans the safely extracted release artifact and a separately materialized GitHub tarball resolved by the already-known commit SHA.
Source tar members are copied as inert regular files without preserving executable modes; links and special files are skipped, and archive limits and traversal checks are enforced.
Trivy findings prefix their target with source: or artifact:, and any exact-source fetch failure makes the required Trivy scanner status failed even when the artifact scan succeeds.

The Semgrep registry presets were not used because they resolve mutable rule content over the network at scan time. Five local syntax-aware rules are vendored instead, and metrics plus version checks are disabled.
Semgrep 1.132.0 is installed as a Python 3.12 uv tool with setuptools 70.3.0 because live validation showed Python 3.14 and current setuptools were incompatible with that Semgrep release.
Semgrep remains optional and every Semgrep result is capped at MANUAL_REVIEW; security-policy enforcement remains report-only.
The Semgrep rules file participates in the workflow audit-cache key so rule edits force a new audit.

verification_evidence.failure_first: Five targeted tests failed before implementation: --config auto remained, source fetch helpers and dual-scan behavior were absent, source hook inertness was unimplemented, and the workflow did not install Semgrep.
verification_evidence.trivy_noop_reproduction: RetroDECKY v1.1.0 release ZIP: Trivy exit 0, lockfiles 0, findings 0.
verification_evidence.trivy_real_source: RetroDECKY v1.1.0 exact commit b2c8e29316757e6999b1698ea57d4582efd6f87b: status found_issue; artifact 0 findings; source 6 findings.
verification_evidence.trivy_known_vulnerability: Trivy 0.73.0 with lodash 4.17.20 package-lock fixture: 5 findings (CVE-2020-28500, CVE-2021-23337, CVE-2025-13465, CVE-2026-2950, CVE-2026-4800).
verification_evidence.source_fetch_failure: Targeted regression test forces _fetch_source_tree to raise and asserts Trivy status failed, no pass, while the artifact scan still runs once.
verification_evidence.nothing_executed: Source tar fixture contains package.json postinstall and setup.py sentinel writers; both files are materialized and the sentinel remains absent.
verification_evidence.semgrep_rules: Semgrep 1.132.0 validated semgrep-rules.yml with 0 configuration errors and 5 rules; invocation excludes --config auto and includes --metrics=off and --disable-version-check.
verification_evidence.semgrep_advisory: Live eval fixture: status found_issue, 1 finding, finding classification MANUAL_REVIEW, aggregate classification MANUAL_REVIEW (never BLOCK).
verification_evidence.semgrep_runtime: RetroDECKY v1.1.0 0.92s; DeckTools v0.6.0 0.98s; Insignia v0.1.2 1.16s. Mean 1.020s; projected 41-plugin cost 41.82s (0.697m), far below doubling the prior approximately 13-minute runtime, so no cadence or timeout mitigation is required.
verification_evidence.quality_gates: Ruff check passed; 37 files already formatted; 256 tests and 21 subtests passed; no deleted review notes.
verification_evidence.catalog_gate: Existing report-only catalog-gate tests remain unchanged; security-policy.yml still sets enforcement.mode to report-only.

test_adjustment_rationale: The audit-verdict test doubles were updated to accept the new source_repo keyword passed to run_trivy. Their scanner statuses and verdict expectations are unchanged; this only reflects the planned interface extension.
not_verified: The live known-CVE assertion is kept out of the hermetic unit suite because Trivy's vulnerability database and installed CLI are external, time-varying inputs. The unit regression instead proves the source scan path contains a pinned lockfile; the live negative control was run separately.
Semgrep's false-positive rate across all 41 plugins remains unmeasured; only three real release artifacts were timed and one synthetic advisory finding was classified.
No claim is made that either scanner proves a plugin benign, detects undeclared vendored dependencies, or justifies enabling catalog enforcement.
